mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, following a period of decline, indicates a nascent recovery trend that will continue to drive retail activity higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, or the week-on-week increase observed at t-0w reverses in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential mobility and a rebound in workplace mobility signals a shift away from home-based activities towards out-of-home work, which will indirectly boost retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 14% AND WORKPLACES rises above -10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, or RESIDENTIAL mobility increases while WORKPLACES mobility decreases in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent rebound in both transit station and workplace mobility indicates a renewed return to commuting patterns, which directly translates to increased foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation areas over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, despite sustained or increased TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in parks mobility at t-0w, coupled with the slight rebound in retail and recreation, suggests an easing of restrictions or a shift in public behavior that will allow for a quick increase in retail activity over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week, or parks mobility rebounds sharply, indicating a reversal of the implied behavioral shift.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low level of grocery and pharmacy mobility, after a significant drop, suggests that residents are no longer prioritizing essential shopping as heavily, freeing up time and resources for discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains below 5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM mobility significantly increases, indicating a return to essential-focused trips.

mechanism_narrative: The significant drop in parks mobility at t-0w indicates a shift away from outdoor leisure, potentially due to weather or other factors, which will redirect discretionary activity towards indoor retail and recreation venues over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week, or PARKS mobility rebounds significantly, indicating a return to outdoor activities.

mechanism_narrative: The observed trend of decreasing residential mobility combined with increasing workplace mobility signifies a broader societal shift back to pre-pandemic routines, driving more people out of their homes and into retail and recreation spaces over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, or the trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL and increasing WORKPLACES mobility reverses.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in parks mobility during a period of generally suppressed retail activity suggests a seasonal transition where outdoor options become less appealing, pushing people towards indoor retail and recreation, leading to an increase over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15% AND RETAIL_REC is below -10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the average of the last 28 days, or PARKS mobility increases significantly, indicating a prolonged outdoor season or renewed interest.
